On the value-type response.Response handler path, leaving Metadata unset causes the HTTP responder to serialize "metadata":null, contrary to the newly documented response-without-metadata format, whic
The added test explicitly expects a response.Response with only Data set to produce a body containing "metadata":null. The updated documentation states that omitted metadata defaults to a JSON object containing only data. The new responder type-switch branch creates its internal response by assigning v.Metadata to an interface{} field; for the unset map this path is demonstrated by the test to encode as null despite the field's omitempty tag.
Impact: Caused by the change: This change adds the response.Response branch at responder.go:31-32 and copies the unset map-valued v.Metadata into the internal interface{} Metadata field. The added without-metadata test records the resulting wire body as "metadata":null. Previously the handler unwrapped response.Response to resp.Data, so this metadata serialization path did not exist; the change therefore introduces the documented-contract mismatch.
